issue: The y-axis label 'Achievable performance' conflicts with the caption's statement that the ceilings are 'peak/theoretical datasheet values, not achieved rates.' A reader can reasonably read 'achievable' as measured or attainable in practice, which is exactly the misconception the caption tries to prevent.
evidence: Y-axis: 'Achievable performance (TFLOPS) — per GPU.' Caption: 'the ceilings are peak/theoretical datasheet values, not achieved rates (sustained MFU is 30–40%, §8.3).' The chart's plateau is a theoretical roofline bound, not an achieved rate.
acceptance_test: Change the y-axis label to 'Theoretical peak performance (TFLOPS)' or 'Roofline bound (TFLOPS)' and ensure the caption and axis use the same scope. Recheck that no prose elsewhere calls the plateau an achieved rate.

figure: FIGURE 8.2 — Per-GPU roofline: dense FP16, one H100 vs one H200
issue: The prefill operating point is drawn and labelled inconsistently with itself, with the caption, and with the facing page. The orange annotation reads (as rendered) 'prefill 9.2K / intensity ≈ 9.2 FLOP/byte', and the orange dotted vertical marker sits only slightly right of the two ridge lines — by my calibration of the log x-axis (10^2 tick at x≈315 px, ≈64 px/decade, confirmed by the ridge markers at 295 and 206) the orange marker is at ≈4×10^2 FLOP/byte, not at 9.2 and not at 9.2×10^3. The caption on the same page says 'Prefill (9.2K input) sits to the right of the compute-bound knee', and PDF 161 (printed 141) says 'Prefill is compute-bound at this scale — its arithmetic intensity sits far above the ridge'. The correct value for the canonical 9.2K-token prefill is 2·N·T / weight-bytes = 2×70e9×9200 / 140e9 ≈ 9.2×10^3 FLOP/byte (≈7.9×10^3 if the 24 GB of KV writes are counted), which is 1.5 decades right of the H100 ridge — i.e. 'far above the ridge', not marginally above it. As drawn, the figure places prefill within a factor of ~1.4 of the knee, which visually undercuts the book's central prefill-vs-decode regime claim.
evidence: Recomputed from the book's own inputs: ridge_H100 = 989e12/3.35e12 = 295 FLOP/byte; ridge_H200 = 989e12/4.8e12 = 206 FLOP/byte (both match the printed labels). Prefill intensity = 2×70e9×9200 FLOP / 140e9 B = 9,200 FLOP/byte. Marker position measured from the rendered page: orange dotted line ≈10^2.6 ≈ 400 FLOP/byte; expected x for 9.2e3 is ≈10^3.96, i.e. ~1.35 decades to the right (≈86 px at 150 dpi). Confidence: the annotation string could not be resolved with certainty at 150 dpi — it may read '9.2K FLOP/byte' rather than '9.2 FLOP/byte'; either reading is inconsistent with the marker position, so the defect is real under both readings.
acceptance_test: Render PDF p.162 at ≥300 dpi and read the annotation string. (a) The annotation must state the prefill intensity in FLOP/byte with the correct magnitude (≈9.2K FLOP/byte, or ≈7.9K if KV writes are included — state which). (b) The orange dotted marker must sit at that x-value on the log axis (≈10^3.96, just left of the 10^4 tick), not at ≈4×10^2. (c) The caption's 'sits to the right of the compute-bound knee' must then be literally true and 'far above the ridge' (PDF 161) must be visually supported. (d) If the intended intensity is ≈400 FLOP/byte, the annotation, the marker, the caption and PDF 161 must all be rewritten together — the four cannot stand as they are.

issue: The y-axis is labelled 'Achievable performance (TFLOPS) — per GPU', but the plotted ceiling is the vendor peak/theoretical datasheet value (the green annotation reads 'compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS'), and the caption explicitly states 'the ceilings are peak/theoretical datasheet values, not achieved runtimes (≈30–40%, 8.5%)'. The axis label therefore asserts the opposite of what the figure plots and what the caption says. A reader who trusts the axis label will read the plateau as a realistic sustained ceiling and will mis-size capacity by roughly 2.5–3×.
evidence: Figure text: y-axis 'Achievable performance (TFLOPS) — per GPU'; plateau annotation 'compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS'; caption 'the ceilings are peak/theoretical datasheet values, not achieved runtimes (≈30–40%, 8.5%)'. 989 TFLOPS is the H100 SXM dense FP16 datasheet peak, not an achieved rate.
acceptance_test: Rename the y-axis to 'Peak (theoretical) performance (TFLOPS) — per GPU' or add '(datasheet peak)' to the axis title, and keep the caption's 'not achieved runtimes' qualifier. Verify that no other figure or table in Ch 8 reuses the phrase 'achievable performance' for a datasheet-peak value.

issue: Two clauses of the caption are not interpretable as printed. (a) 'Convention: a multiply-add counts as 2 FLOPs; the FMA convention of 8,1: dense (no sparsity) FP16' — the token '8,1' is not a meaningful quantity and the sentence has already fixed the convention in its first clause, so the fragment appears to be a corrupted number. (b) 'the plotted prefill (9.2K input) and decode (batch=1) points are illustrative operating points, and a kernel's latency — not measured SLO-goodput.' — the trailing clause has no verb and no predicate; the intended contrast (these are kernel-latency points, not measured SLO-goodput) is not stated. Both are in the caption that is the figure's only interpretive key.
evidence: Caption text as rendered on PDF p.162: 'Convention: a multiply-add counts as 2 FLOPs; the FMA convention of 8,1: dense (no sparsity) FP16; ... and a kernel's latency — not measured SLO-goodput.' Confidence: the characters '8,1' could not be resolved with certainty at 150 dpi (candidates: '8,1', '8:1', '2,1'); the defect is that the clause does not parse under any reading.
acceptance_test: Repair both clauses in the source. Suggested: 'Convention: a multiply-add counts as 2 FLOPs; dense (no sparsity) FP16; the ceilings are peak/theoretical datasheet values, not achieved runtimes (≈30–40%, 8.5%); the plotted prefill and decode points are illustrative kernel-level operating points, not measured SLO-goodput.' Re-read the caption aloud against the rendered page to confirm every clause parses.

issue: The caption says 'decode (batch=1) sits to the left, on the memory-bound slope; and decode (batched=1) sits to the left, on the memory-bound slope and continuous batching climbs the slope as batch grows'. The same predicate ('sits to the left') is applied to two points the figure draws at different positions, and the intended reading ('to the left of the knee') is never stated. The caption also never gives the batch size or the resulting arithmetic intensity for the batched point, so the reader cannot check the plotted marker. The label 'decode (batched=1)' is itself ambiguous — it reads as 'batch = 1' rather than 'batched decode'.
evidence: Recomputed decode intensities for the canonical 70B at FP16: batch=1 → 2·N / (2N + KV) ≈ 1.0 FLOP/byte (weights dominate: 1.4e11 FLOP/token ÷ 1.4e11 B/token), which places the batch=1 marker at 10^0 on the log axis — consistent with the figure's leftmost marker. Batched decode at batch B moves right along the slope (intensity ≈ B for small B), so the batched marker must be to the RIGHT of the batch=1 marker and still left of the 295 ridge for B ≲ 100. The caption's 'climbs the slope as batch grows' is consistent with this, but 'sits to the left' is not.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption clause as: 'decode (batch=1, intensity ≈1 FLOP/byte) sits far left on the memory-bound slope; batched decode (batch B, intensity ≈B FLOP/byte) climbs that slope toward the knee, reaching the knee only at B ≈ 295 for H100.' Rename the figure annotation 'decode batched' to 'decode batch B (batched)' and label the plotted batched point with its batch size and intensity so the reader can verify its x-position.

issue: The x-axis appears to label only 10⁻¹, 10⁰, 10¹, 10² and 10⁴, with the 10³ decade label missing. If so, the decade in which the prefill marker should sit (≈9.2×10³, see F-01) is unlabelled, which is both a plotting defect and an obstacle to the reader checking the prefill position.
evidence: Rendered x-axis tick labels: 10⁻¹, 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10⁴. Confidence: a 10³ label may exist but be unresolvable at 150 dpi; the axis range and the ridge markers both imply a decade grid at 10³.
acceptance_test: Render PDF p.162 at ≥300 dpi and confirm the 10³ label is present. If it is absent, add it (or label every decade) so that the prefill marker at ≈9.2×10³ can be located by the reader.

issue: The caption enumerates the plotted points as 'the plotted prefill (9.2K input) and decode (batch=1) points are illustrative operating points', but the figure plots three annotated points — prefill, decode batch=1, and decode batched. acceptance_test: Extend the caption list to 'the plotted prefill, decode (batch=1) and decode (batched) points are illustrative operating points', and give the batched point a batch size and intensity in both the figure annotation and the caption so that its x-position is checkable.

issue: The two ridge markers are vertical dotted lines separated by only about 10 px at 150 dpi (≈0.15 in at print size), and their labels 'ridge = 295' and 'ridge = 206' are stacked immediately to the left of them. Because both markers are dotted and differ only in colour, a reader can easily attach the upper label to the wrong line, and in grayscale the two markers are nearly identical. The quantitative difference between the two ridges (295 vs 206) is one of the chapter's key points (H200's higher bandwidth moves the knee left), so the association must be unambiguous.
evidence: Rendered page: blue dotted vertical line at x ≈ 340 px, red dotted vertical line at x ≈ 330 px; labels 'ridge = 295' (blue) and 'ridge = 206' (red) stacked at x ≈ 300–345. The curves themselves are solid (H100) vs dashed (H200), which is the only unambiguous cue.
acceptance_test: Make the two ridge markers distinguishable without colour (e.g. solid for H100, dashed for H200, matching the curve styles) and place each label immediately adjacent to its own line with a short leader, or label them 'H100 ridge = 295' and 'H200 ridge = 206'. Confirm on a grayscale 300-dpi render that each label is unambiguously attached to its line.

issue: Color legend states 'Blue: data/state. Orange: compute' but two blue-outlined boxes label computational models/processes, not data objects, so the stated rule does not apply to every box.
evidence: Legend at figure bottom: 'Blue: data/state. Orange: compute.' Box 'UMT5-XXL / ≤512 prompt tokens' is blue-outlined; box 'VAE encode / I2V condition only' is blue-outlined. Both label models/processes (compute), not data. Orange boxes are 'Wan2.2 dense Ti2V-5B + scheduler' and 'VAE decode' — both compute. The blue/orange split does not consistently separate data from compute as the legend claims.
acceptance_test: Either (a) relabel blue boxes with data names (e.g., 'Text embeddings (≤512 tokens)', 'Image features (I2V)'), (b) recolor UMTT5-XXL and VAE encode orange and add separate blue data boxes for their outputs, or (c) revise legend to 'Blue: data/state and input preprocessing. Orange: denoising compute.' Verify the revised legend rule applies to every box without exception.

issue: The legend says blue = data/state and orange = compute, but UMT5-XXL and VAE encode are compute modules and are colored blue. This makes the visual encoding inconsistent with the legend and obscures which boxes are computation versus data.
evidence: Legend: 'Blue: data/state. Orange: compute.' The 'UMT5-XXL ≤512 prompt tokens' box and the 'VAE encode I2V condition only' box are blue, although both are neural-network compute modules. By contrast, 'Wan2.2 dense TI2V-5B + scheduler' and 'VAE decode' are orange.
acceptance_test: Recolor UMT5-XXL and VAE encode as compute (orange), or introduce and label a third category such as 'conditioning encoder' with its own legend entry. Verify that every box's color matches its role and that the legend explains all colors used.

issue: The legend contains the sentence 'Token partitioning adds communication between devices,' but no visual symbol or annotation depicts token partitioning or inter-device communication. The legend is therefore carrying prose that does not explain any visual encoding.
evidence: Legend text: 'Solid: data/state flow. Dashed: denoiser conditioning. Blue: data/state. Orange: compute. Token partitioning adds communication between devices.' No box, arrow, or symbol in the diagram represents token partitioning or communication.
acceptance_test: Either add a visual symbol/annotation for token partitioning and inter-device communication, or move the sentence to the caption as a scope note. The legend should contain only keys that map to visible encodings.

issue: The data/state vs compute distinction is encoded only by box fill hue (pale blue vs pale peach). In a grayscale print both become near-identical light-gray fills with similar gray borders and no differing fill pattern or border weight, so the two categories are not visually distinguishable without color, violating the 'do not rely on color alone / must remain interpretable in grayscale' rule. Rated MINOR (not MAJOR) because each box's title still identifies its role, so the figure remains interpretable in grayscale via text rather than via the color encoding.
evidence: Rendered page: 'Prompt', 'UMT5-XXL', 'VAE encode', 'Latent: T x H x W x C', and the bottom output box use a pale-blue fill; the 'Wan2.2 dense TI2V-5B + scheduler' and 'VAE decode' boxes use a pale-peach fill. The footnote states 'Blue: data/state. Orange: compute.' Neither fill carries a hatch/dot pattern and the borders are the same weight, so a grayscale render collapses the two categories to the same light gray. (The solid/dashed line semantics for flow type are grayscale-safe and are not the issue.)
acceptance_test: Add a non-hue cue separating the two box categories — e.g., a subtle fill pattern (dots/hatch) on the compute boxes, a heavier or double border on one category, or a small icon — and confirm in a grayscale render that a reader can tell data/state from compute using the legend without color. Keep the existing solid = data/state flow and dashed = denoiser conditioning line semantics unchanged.

issue: The VAE-decode box prints the frame-count derivation as 'Aligned endpoint: 1 × 4 × (31 − 1) = 121 frames'. As rendered, the operator between '1' and '4' is a multiplication sign, and 1 × 4 × 30 = 120, not 121 — the equation contradicts the number printed immediately after it and the number printed in the output box ('121 frames'). The correct derivation for a stride-4 temporal VAE is 1 + 4 × (31 − 1) = 121 (the +1 accounts for the first frame). The caption repeats the correct total ('31 latent time positions correspond to 121 frames'), so the figure and the caption currently disagree on the arithmetic.
evidence: Independent recomputation: (31 − 1) × 4 + 1 = 121 ✓; 1 × 4 × (31 − 1) = 120 ✗. Cross-check of the same figure's other arithmetic: patch (1,2,2) over latent 31×44×80 → 31 × 22 × 40 = 27,280 tokens ✓ (matches 'N = 27,280 video tokens'); VAE stride (4,16,16) → 44×16 = 704 ✓ and 80×16 = 1,280 ✓ (matches the output box). Confidence: the glyph could not be resolved with certainty at 150 dpi — it may be '+' rather than '×'; the finding is that the printed equation must be checked, because as rendered it evaluates to 120.
acceptance_test: Render PDF p.167 at ≥300 dpi and confirm the operator in 'Aligned endpoint: 1 ? 4 × (31 − 1) = 121 frames'. If it is '×', change it to '1 + 4 × (31 − 1) = 121 frames'. If it is '+', no change is needed to the equation, but the caption's parallel statement should be made to show the same form so the two are visibly identical.

issue: The legend states 'Solid: data/state flow. Dashed: denoiser conditioning.' But the figure's dashed feedback loop on the right of the 'Wan2.2 dense T2V-5B + scheduler' box is the denoising/scheduler iteration — a control-flow loop, not conditioning — and the caption says so explicitly ('The feedback loop is denoising/scheduler iteration, not architectural recurrence'). A reader applying the legend literally will read the dashed loop as 'conditioning', i.e. as a second conditioning input, which is a different mechanism entirely. The figure therefore uses one visual channel (dash pattern) for two distinct semantic classes.
evidence: Legend line under FIG 8.3: 'Solid: data/state flow. Dashed: denoiser conditioning. Blue: data/state. Orange: compute. Token partitioning adds communication between devices.' Dashed elements in the drawing: (i) UMT5-XXL → denoiser, (ii) VAE encode → denoiser, (iii) the right-hand loop arrow from the denoiser box back into itself. Caption: 'The feedback loop is denoising/scheduler iteration, not architectural recurrence.'
acceptance_test: Give the iteration loop a distinct dash pattern (e.g. dotted, or a dash-dot) and extend the legend to three entries: 'Solid: data/state flow. Dashed: denoiser conditioning. Dotted: scheduler iteration (control flow).' Confirm that after the change no dashed element other than the two conditioning arrows remains.

issue: Two caption fragments are not interpretable as printed. (a) 'The fetched implementation uses T_I2V=1/4=1, H_I2V=16, and W_I2V=16.' — 'T_I2V=1/4=1' chains two equalities with no defined quantity; the figure's own box says 'VAE stride (T, H, W) = (4, 16, 16)', so the caption and the figure express the same fact in two incompatible forms. (b) 'For aligned F_φk=1, F_φk+1, F_φk+1=1: 31 latent time positions correspond to 121 frames.' — the subscript sequence appears duplicated ('F_φk+1' twice) and the condition it states is not connected to the 121-frame derivation.
evidence: Caption text as rendered on PDF p.167; figure box text 'VAE stride (T, H, W) = (4, 16, 16)' and 'Aligned endpoint: 1 ? 4 × (31 − 1) = 121 frames'. Confidence: the subscript glyphs could not be resolved with certainty at 150 dpi; the defect is that neither fragment parses.
acceptance_test: Rewrite both fragments so that each quantity is defined once and used consistently with the figure: e.g. 'the fetched implementation uses a temporal compression factor of 4 and spatial factors of 16 (VAE stride (T,H,W) = (4,16,16))' and 'for the aligned first/last-frame factors, 31 latent time positions correspond to 1 + 4 × (31 − 1) = 121 frames'. Confirm the caption and the figure boxes use identical symbols.

figure: FIGURE 8.3 — 'VAE encode I2V condition only' box
issue: The 'VAE encode I2V condition only' box is filled blue, which the legend defines as 'data/state', although the box is a compute stage (a VAE encode pass). The sibling 'VAE decode' box is orange ('compute') even though it also terminates in a data artifact. The colour rule is therefore applied inconsistently between two structurally identical stages, and a reader may infer that the I2V condition path involves no compute.

Boxes: 'VAE encode I2V condition only' = blue; 'VAE decode' = orange; 'Wan2.2 dense T2V-5B + scheduler' = orange; 'Prompt', 'Optional reference image', 'Initial noise (FP32)', 'UMT5-XXL s512 prompt tokens', 'Latent: T×H×W×C', '121 frames · 704×1280 · 24 fps' = blue.
acceptance_test: Either recolour 'VAE encode I2V condition only' orange and state the rule as 'orange = compute stage, blue = data artifact', or add a legend note that blue marks data artifacts regardless of the stage that produces them. Confirm the rule is applied consistently to both VAE boxes.

figure: FIGURE 8.3 — legend line and in-box annotations
issue: The legend line ('Solid: data/state flow. Dashed: denoiser conditioning. Blue: data/state. Orange: compute. Token partitioning adds communication between devices.') and the sub-lines inside the orange boxes ('Patch (1, 2, 2): N = 27,280 video tokens', '50 steps × 2 CFG branch evaluations', 'Loop: denoising / scheduler iteration', 'VAE stride (T, H, W) = (4, 16, 16)', 'Aligned endpoint: 1 ? 4 × (31 − 1) = 121 frames') render smaller than the figure's box titles and appear to sit at or below the 8 pt floor for figure in-text annotations. This needs a measurement rather than an eyeball judgement.
evidence: Rendered page: the legend line and the in-box sub-lines are visibly smaller than the box titles ('Wan2.2 dense T2V-5B + scheduler', 'VAE decode', '121 frames · 704 (H) × 1280 (W) · 24 fps').
acceptance_test: Measure the rendered type size of the legend line and the in-box sub-lines at 100% on the printed page; all must be ≥ 8 pt. If any is below, raise it to 8 pt and re-check that the boxes still fit without crowding.

figure: Figure 9.1 — Ring traffic and directional bandwidth
issue: The figure note says 'no offload, latency or overlap', but the plotted 544 ms value depends on concurrent send and receive (overlap of the two directions). The note can therefore be read as contradicting the model used to produce the curve.
evidence: Caption: 'Each rank sends 1.75 times the logical tensor size and receives the same amount. Curves use 450 GB/s ...'. Prose on printed p. 156: 'With concurrent send and receive, its ideal time is T_ring ≈ 245/450 ≈ 0.54 s. Equivalently, 490 GB of sent-plus-received traffic divided by 900 GB/s gives the same time.' Figure note: 'Analytical model; no offload, latency or overlap; not measured.' If 'overlap' meant no send/receive overlap, the time would be 490/450 ≈ 1.09 s, not 0.54 s.
acceptance_test: Revise the note to say 'no offload, latency, or communication/computation overlap' (or equivalent), so it cannot be read as denying the concurrent send/receive assumption behind the plotted times.

figure: Figure 9.1 — Ring traffic and directional bandwidth
issue: The caption does not state the time formula used for the curves. A reader can see 'sent bytes per rank = 1.75 × tensor bytes' and 'ideal ring completion time' but is not told that the plotted time is sent bytes per rank divided by directional bandwidth, with send and receive concurrent.
evidence: Subtitle: 'sent bytes per rank = 1.75 × tensor bytes'. Caption: 'Each rank sends 1.75 times the logical tensor size and receives the same amount. Curves use 450 GB/s ...'. The caption never says 'time = sent bytes per rank / directional bandwidth' or 'assuming concurrent send and receive'. The prose on p. 156 supplies this, but the figure caption should be self-contained.
acceptance_test: Add one clause to the caption: 'Plotted time is sent bytes per rank divided by directional bandwidth, assuming concurrent send and receive.'

issue: The bottom annotation 'Analytical model; no offload, latency or overlap; not measured' uses the word 'overlap' ambiguously. The plotted 1.75x factor (subtitle line 1: 'sent bytes per rank = 1.75 x tensor bytes') and the prose on p.161 ('With concurrent send and receive') both assume full-duplex send/receive overlap *within* each phase, while the two phases (reduce-scatter, all-gather) are sequential. Read in isolation, 'no overlap' can be misread as negating send/receive concurrency, which would contradict the figure's own arithmetic: a half-duplex (no send/receive overlap) ring would require 3.5x M/B, not the 1.75x M/B that every curve on the plot follows. So the annotation, sitting inside the same figure that displays the 1.75x factor, is internally in tension with that factor.
evidence: At 140 GB the NVLink marker is 544 ms = 245/450 = 1.75*140/450, a value that only holds with concurrent send+receive; all three curves are straight slope-1 lines on the log-log axes passing through 1.75*M/B with no alpha floor, confirming the model is bytes-only and full-duplex. Prose PDF 181 / printed 161 states explicitly: 'With concurrent send and receive, its ideal time is T_ring ~ 245/450 ~ 0.54 s. Equivalently, 490 GB of sent-plus-received traffic divided by 900 GB/s gives the same time.' The figure's 'no overlap' is not reconciled with this in either the annotation or the caption.
acceptance_test: Reword the annotation so 'overlap' is unambiguous, e.g. 'Analytical model; no collective offload, no per-step latency (alpha), communication not overlapped with computation; send/receive full-duplex assumed; not measured.' After the change, a reader viewing only the figure cannot infer a half-duplex (3.5x) model, and the annotation no longer appears to contradict the 1.75x factor printed in the same figure's subtitle.

issue: The subtitle says '140 GB tensor' while the x-axis says 'Logical input tensor per rank [GB]'; the per-rank qualifier is dropped exactly where the reader needs it to interpret the 1.75× factor.
evidence: Subtitle: 'N = 8; sent bytes per rank = 1.75 × tensor bytes / 140 GB tensor (245 GB sent at 1.75×)'. X-axis: 'Logical input tensor per rank [GB]'. Caption: 'Each rank sends 1.75 times the logical tensor size'. A reader who takes '140 GB tensor' as the whole collective payload would expect 1.75 × 140/8 GB per rank, not 245 GB.
acceptance_test: Change the subtitle to '140 GB per rank (245 GB sent at 1.75×)' so that the subtitle, the x-axis, and the caption use one qualifier.

issue: The figure asserts the 1.75× traffic factor without showing where it comes from, so the reader must take it on faith or reconstruct it from the caption.
evidence: Subtitle: 'sent bytes per rank = 1.75 × tensor bytes'. The factor is 2(N−1)/N = 2×7/8 = 1.75 for N=8 (reduce-scatter plus all-gather, each moving (N−1)/N of the tensor). Neither the figure nor the caption states this; the caption only says 'Each rank sends 1.75 times the logical tensor size and receives the same amount.' The same unexplained constant appears in FIG 9.2 as '12 B sent' for an 8 B input (1.5× at N=4).
acceptance_test: Add the derivation to the subtitle, e.g. 'sent bytes per rank = 2(N−1)/N × tensor = 1.75 × tensor bytes', and mirror the same form in FIG 9.2's summary box ('12 B sent = 1.5 × 8 B input').
